items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: Hallwood said they hired me at that time because of the war

ctx.x: Then I had a lot of pupils. I was doing very good teaching and then I was working on the staff, too. Then finally Hank D'Amico and Vernon Brown and Billy Butterfield and a bunch of them came over on the staff and they all were playing with Paul Lavalle so I was playing with them. Then finally they gave Hank a band and I was the arranger. And I wrote a lot of things for that station while I was up there.

And then finally -- Hallwood said they hired me at that time because of the war, you know, and they wanted to make it look good that they had -- I was the only Negro in there, you know. They wanted to make it look good. So when the war was over, 1946 it was when I got my notice with 25 other men -- got their notice. And everybody was eventually hired back but me. And "Down Beat" had it in the paper, they said, well, with Barefield's seniority he should fight this. And I got a lot of calls to take up -- go back…
And I was busy. I went from there to WOR with Cy Oliver doing the Dorsey Show. And that was good. And then
